title: Canned Motor Pump

introduction.definition: A canned motor pump combines pump and motor in one hermetically sealed unit: the motor rotor runs in the pumped liquid inside a thin "can", and the stator is sealed from the liquid by a stator liner. Part of the pumped liquid circulates through the motor to cool it and lubricate the bearings.
introduction.summary: The motor rotor and the pump impeller are on one shaft inside a fully enclosed pressure boundary. The stator windings are sealed from the pumped liquid by a thin stator liner (can); the rotor is sealed by its own can. A small flow of pumped liquid circulates through the motor gap to remove heat and lubricate the sleeve bearings. There is no shaft seal and no coupling, so leakage paths are eliminated; the motor housing gives secondary containment.

parts.name: Volute Casing
parts.function: Collects flow leaving the impeller and converts velocity into pressure in a spiral passage of increasing area, then discharges through a diffuser nozzle.
parts.material: Cast iron, ductile iron, carbon steel, stainless steel (CF8M), duplex.

parts.name: Closed Impeller
parts.function: Adds energy to the liquid; blades between hub and shrouds accelerate the liquid outward.
parts.material: Cast iron, bronze, stainless steel (CF8M, CA6NM), duplex.

parts.name: Adapter & Front Bearing Housing
parts.function: Connects casing to motor and houses the front bearing.

parts.name: Motor Housing (Secondary Containment)
parts.function: Holds the stator and provides secondary containment if the stator liner fails.

parts.name: Stator Core & Windings
parts.material: Silicon electrical steel, copper magnet wire, Class F/H insulation (typical).

parts.name: Stator Liner (Stator Can)
parts.function: Thin can that separates the stator windings from the pumped liquid.

parts.name: Canned Rotor & Shaft
parts.function: Squirrel-cage rotor sealed in its own can; carries the impeller on the common shaft.

parts.name: Product-Lubricated Journal Bearings
parts.function: Support the rotor/impeller shaft, lubricated by the pumped liquid.

parts.name: Rear Bearing Housing & End Cover
parts.function: Closes the motor end, houses the rear bearing and returns circulation flow.

parts.name: Bearing Wear Monitor
parts.function: Indicates bearing wear (rotor position) so the pump can be stopped before the cans are damaged.

parts.name: Circulation Line (Discharge to Motor)
parts.function: Takes a small flow from discharge through the motor for cooling and bearing lubrication.

parts.name: Baseplate
parts.function: Provides a rigid common mounting for pump and driver, maintains alignment and transfers loads to the foundation.
parts.material: Carbon steel, painted; stainless steel for hygienic or corrosive areas.

piping: Support suction and discharge piping independently so nozzle loads stay within the manufacturer's (or API 610/HI 9.6.2) allowable values.
Provide a straight run of at least 5 pipe diameters ahead of the suction nozzle (ANSI/HI 9.6.6 guidance — verify) and use an eccentric reducer with the flat side up.

script.narration: This module introduces the Canned Motor Pump.
A canned motor pump combines pump and motor in one hermetically sealed unit: the motor rotor runs in the pumped liquid inside a thin "can", and the stator is sealed from the liquid by a stator liner.
Part of the pumped liquid circulates through the motor to cool it and lubricate the bearings.
Typical applications include hazardous and toxic chemicals; refrigeration and ammonia; heat-transfer oils; nuclear and high-pressure systems.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Volute Casing, Closed Impeller, Adapter & Front Bearing Housing, Canned Rotor & Shaft.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Canned Motor Pump.
Check bearing monitor and motor temperature.
Check circulation line.
Replace bearings when the monitor indicates wear.
Watch for bearing wear: bearing monitor alarm. Common cause: dry running, solids.
Watch for overheating: thermal trip. Common cause: blocked circulation, vaporisation.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
